stemBlocks.value: OLMN is a quadrilateral with O the origin, OL = 4y, OM = 6z and ON = 2x. A lies on LM with LA : AM = 1 : 2, and B lies on MN with MB : BN = 2 : 1. (vi) Express MN in terms of x and z. (vii) a) Find LN in terms of x and y. b) Show that AB = (2/3)(2x − 4y). (viii) State TWO geometric properties relating LN to AB.
Think first: Everything is measured from the origin O, so any vector PQ is simply OQ − OP — build each answer that way before touching the ratios.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p279-q02 from workbook page 279.

solutionSteps.instruction: Subtract the position vectors of M and N.
Do the same for L and N.
Find LM, then take the part of it from A to M. Since LA : AM = 1 : 2, AM is two-thirds of LM.
Find MB, which is two-thirds of MN since MB : BN = 2 : 1.
Add AM and MB to travel from A to B, and factor the result.

contentBlocks.value: Result: AB is parallel to LN and AB is two-thirds the length of LN

strategyBlocks.value: Get MN and LN by subtracting position vectors, then reach B by travelling A → M → B, using AM = (2/3)LM and MB = (2/3)MN, and finally compare AB with LN.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (vi) MN = 2x − 6z  (vii) a) LN = 2x − 4y  b) AB = AM + MB = (4z − (8/3)y) + ((4/3)x − 4z) = (4/3)x − (8/3)y = (2/3)(2x − 4y)  (viii) AB is parallel to LN (same direction), and AB is two-thirds the length of LN, i.e. |AB| : |LN| = 2 : 3.

whyThisWorks.value: With O as origin every point has a position vector, so the vector from one point to another is always 'finish minus start'. A ratio along a segment converts into a fraction of that segment's vector, letting you land exactly on A and B. When the final expression for AB turns out to be a number times LN, that number carries both facts at once: the direction is unchanged (parallel) and the length is scaled by that number.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing MN = OM − ON, reversing the direction.

commonErrors.misconception: Using LA = (2/3)LM instead of AM = (2/3)LM — the ratio 1 : 2 puts A nearer L.
